notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS startup building a developer-facing code assistance product and in-app support bot.
- Initially attracted to Redwood for predictable latency, routing and dedicated capacity options.
- PoC ran for 6 weeks (Nov–Dec 2024); used small fleet on hosted API, tested code-assist prompts + reranking.
Key quotes/feedback:
- CTO: 'We need plug-and-play with minimal ops burden' — primary driver was engineering velocity.
- Lead engineer: liked Redwood batching + routing but said 'OpenAI just works with less setup'.
Procurement & business context:
- Procurement team prefers vendor with clear public pricing and broad community docs.
- Internal budget freeze in early Jan 2025 slowed negotiations — deprioritized rollout.
Technical/security findings:
- Security review: required SSO (SAML), audit logging, SOC2. Redwood met most items but team perceived additional integration work for private deployment.
- No data residency requirement but wanted clear audit trail and KMS support.
Champion/org dynamics:
- Original champion (senior engineer) left company in Jan; no replacement champion surfaced.\- Sales motion: AE introduced Redwood Dedicated; SE supported with benchmark report (see Drive link).
Outcome & why lost:
- Decision: adopt OpenAI direct API for initial launch. Reasons: simpler onboarding, perceived brand reliability by product org, and lower perceived ops cost. Budget freeze also pushed them to the lowest-friction path.
Next steps (internal):
- Mark opportunity closed-lost and file WIN/LOSS doc to Drive link.
- Request post-mortem with AE + SE for notes on tackling brand preference and friction.
- Keep 6–9 month cadence for re-engagement (target org hire / champion reappears).
